references.text: The place was called Massah and Meribah because the Israelites quarreled with the Lord. This refers to the earlier event at Meribah mentioned in Numbers 20:13.
Moses and Aaron were unfaithful to the Lord at the waters of Meribah in Kadesh in the wilderness of Zin, and did not honor him as holy among the Israelites.
At Meribah the people put the Lord to the test, and Moses' faithfulness was tried.
The psalm mentions that God tested Israel at the waters of Meribah, a direct reference to the event in Numbers 20.
A warning not to harden your hearts as at Meribah, where the fathers tempted God.
At the waters of Meribah they provoked the Lord's anger, and it went badly for Moses on their account. They made his spirit bitter.
The Lord says he will sanctify himself among his people, just as he sanctified himself at the waters of Meribah.
The Lord declares that he will sanctify himself and be known among the nations, linking to the theme of God's holiness in Numbers 20:13.
Hebrews quotes Psalm 95 and warns against hardening hearts as on the day of testing in the wilderness, a reference to the Meribah event.
